title: Texas Tribune: FBI Lab Tests Find No Meth in Salgado Araujo Van, Undermining DHS Narrative
excerpt: The U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas confirmed that FBI laboratory tests found no methamphetamine in the van driven by Lorenzo Salgado Araujo when he was fatally shot by an ICE officer in Houston on July 7. The negative result contradicted a search warrant affidavit that the FBI had made public unusually fast, which critics said appeared aimed at discrediting the victim and witnesses.
content:
On August 13, 2026, U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz confirmed to The Texas Tribune that FBI laboratory tests on a "white crystal-like substance" found in the van of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo—fatally shot by an ICE officer in Houston on July 7, 2026—were negative for methamphetamine.

The FBI had sought a search warrant on July 14, one week after the shooting, suggesting the substance could be meth. Critics noted the search warrant affidavit was made public the day after it was filed—unusually fast—and accused the government of attempting to taint the victim's and witnesses' reputations ahead of any trial. The negative test results, by contrast, were withheld for nearly a month.

  • Passengers in the van said the bags contained salt that the construction workers mixed with water and lemon to stay hydrated during hot Texas summers.
  • U.S. Rep. Sylvia Garcia (D-TX), the Harris County District Attorney, and the Salgado family's attorney had all insisted the substance was salt.
  • The U.S. Attorney did not reveal what substance was actually found, and the FBI cited the ongoing investigation in declining to release full results—despite the search warrant having been made public immediately after filing.
  • Reitz's office did not respond to questions about whether the full test results would be made public.
"I can confirm what's already public: lab testing showed the substance in the baggies was not meth." — U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz, Southern District of Texas
